tests/01-setup.test.ts.title: CLIENT_SETUP <-> SERVER_SETUP round-trip against a live relay.
tests/01-setup.test.ts.description:
Both profiles are exercised because the setup path is identical for
stream vs datagram tracks — this test just proves auth + version
negotiation work end-to-end.

tests/02-announce.test.ts.title: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE (announce) round-trip against a live relay.
tests/02-announce.test.ts.description:
A publisher-side session issues `announceNamespace()` and expects the
relay to reply with REQUEST_OK. `announceNamespace()` only resolves once
the ack arrives, so a successful await proves the exchange happened.

tests/03-publish.test.ts.title: PUBLISH round-trip against a live relay.
tests/03-publish.test.ts.description:
`session.publish()` sends PUBLISH on a per-request bidi stream (draft-18)
and resolves with the assigned track alias after REQUEST_OK. If the
relay rejects the request the promise rejects. A resolved bigint alias
proves the exchange succeeded.

tests/04-subscribe-namespace.test.ts.title: SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE bidirectional flow.
tests/04-subscribe-namespace.test.ts.description:
Session B subscribes to a namespace prefix. Session A then announces a
track under that prefix; the relay must fan the announcement out to B,
which raises the `incoming-publish` event. That event is the signal that
subscribe-namespace matched. Covers the incoming-subscribe / incoming-
publish surface without requiring a live media flow.

tests/05-subscribe.test.ts.title: End-to-end pub/sub against a live relay.
tests/05-subscribe.test.ts.description:
Session A publishes a chat track under a unique namespace.
Session B subscribes to the same track.
Every object B receives must byte-match what A sent. On a stream all of
them must arrive, in order; datagrams are not retransmitted, so up to 10%
may be lost and the report lists which.

tests/06-subscribe-update.test.ts.title: SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE / REQUEST_UPDATE pause+resume flow.
tests/06-subscribe-update.test.ts.description:
Publisher streams a chat track. Subscriber pauses after receiving a few
objects, expects the incoming object stream to quiesce, then resumes and
expects more objects to arrive. This exercises the draft-18
REQUEST_UPDATE(forward=0/1) path.

tests/07-unsubscribe.test.ts.title: UNSUBSCRIBE round-trip.
tests/07-unsubscribe.test.ts.description:
Subscribe to a live track, receive some objects, unsubscribe, and
confirm no further deliveries arrive after a settle period.

tests/08-track-status.test.ts.title: TRACK_STATUS round-trip (draft-18 only).
tests/08-track-status.test.ts.description:
A publisher advertises a track, and a second session queries its status.
`trackStatus()` resolves when the relay returns REQUEST_OK; it throws on
REQUEST_ERROR. Both outcomes prove the exchange is wire-correct — the
strict requirement is just that the promise settles without a timeout.

tests/09-fetch.test.ts.title: FETCH historical retrieval.
tests/09-fetch.test.ts.description:
A publisher streams objects into the relay's cache; a second session
FETCHes a subrange and expects to receive the same bytes back for
every (group, object) in that range.

Not every relay honors FETCH for arbitrary tracks. When the relay
responds with REQUEST_ERROR the harness catches the FETCH error event
and marks the test as skipped so we still surface protocol coverage.

tests/10-fetch-cancel.test.ts.title: FETCH_CANCEL flow.
tests/10-fetch-cancel.test.ts.description:
Kick off a fetch that would return many objects, cancel it as soon as
we've received at least one, and confirm the count stops climbing.
As with 09-fetch, the test tolerates relays that do not support FETCH
by skipping when FETCH itself errors out.

tests/11-goaway.test.ts.title: GOAWAY graceful shutdown (draft-18 only).
tests/11-goaway.test.ts.description:
The client issues GOAWAY; the session transitions to 'closing' locally.
This is a lightweight surface test — we don't require the relay to echo
anything back, just that the client encoder produces a wire-valid GOAWAY
and drives its own state machine forward.

tests/12-session-close.test.ts.title: Session termination code (draft-18 §15.10.1).
tests/12-session-close.test.ts.description:
`session.close({ code, reason })` should pass the numeric SessionErrorCode
down to the underlying WebTransport `close({ closeCode })`. We drive both
the graceful NO_ERROR path and a synthetic PROTOCOL_VIOLATION path; the
relay is not required to echo anything back — this test just proves the
client plumbs the code through and the local state machine transitions.

tests/13-session-termination.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §3.5 inbound Session Termination + §3.6 Migration surface tests.
tests/13-session-termination.test.ts.description:
These tests don't require the relay to actively terminate or issue GOAWAY
with a `newSessionUri` — we drive the client-side event plumbing via the
private `handleIncomingGoAwayDraft18` path and via `session.close()`. That
proves:
  - the `session-terminated` event exists and does not fire for local closes
  - GOAWAY with a `newSessionUri` populates `pendingMigrationUri`
  - `migrate()` rejects with a clear error in main-thread mode

A full over-the-wire migration test needs coordinated dual-relay support and
is out of scope for the browser CI matrix; see docs/draft-18-interop-plan.md.

tests/14-setup-extensions.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §3.2 SETUP extension advertisement — end-to-end surface tests.
tests/14-setup-extensions.test.ts.description:
Draft-18 says: peers MUST ignore unknown SETUP extensions. So we can safely
advertise a client extension with an unregistered key and verify the relay
still completes SERVER_SETUP.

These tests don't rely on the relay advertising any specific extensions —
`peerExtensions` may be undefined depending on the relay build. We only
assert (a) the client can inject extensions without breaking the setup
round-trip, and (b) the getter is populated whenever the relay does send
some.

tests/15-track-status-largest.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §10.14 TRACK_STATUS + §10.2.9 LARGEST_OBJECT — end-to-end shape.
tests/15-track-status-largest.test.ts.description:
We publish a track, send several objects on it, then issue a TRACK_STATUS
query from a second session. The relay is not required to forward the
query to our publisher session — some relay implementations answer status
queries themselves — so this test asserts:
  1. `trackStatus()` resolves to a `TrackStatusResult` (or throws a
     REQUEST_ERROR that the test tolerates);
  2. when `latestGroup`/`latestObject` are present, both are `bigint` and
     non-negative, matching the wire semantics.

The strict semantics — LARGEST_OBJECT matches the last object we sent —
are covered by the unit tests in `session-track-status.test.ts`; here we
only prove the request/response mechanism doesn't break end-to-end.

tests/16-namespace-done.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §10.17 NAMESPACE_DONE end-of-batch signal.
tests/16-namespace-done.test.ts.description:
A subscriber issues SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE against a prefix. The relay
responds with REQUEST_OK, streams any matching NAMESPACE messages, and
closes the batch with NAMESPACE_DONE — that terminal frame is what we
assert here.

We tolerate either outcome:
  1. `namespace-done` fires within the timeout (relay honors §10.17);
  2. no NAMESPACE_DONE arrives — some relays keep the stream open for
     future NAMESPACE fan-out, which is also spec-permissible. We only
     fail if the SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE itself never resolves.

tests/17-subscribe-tracks.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §10.19 SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS end-to-end.
tests/17-subscribe-tracks.test.ts.description:
Publisher A opens a session and announces a track under a namespace.
Subscriber B calls `subscribeTracks(prefix)` with the full param set
(FORWARD + SUBSCRIPTION_FILTER). We assert the request resolves — the
relay parsed our extended parameter list and issued REQUEST_OK. Deeper
per-parameter round-trip is covered by the unit + codec tests.

tests/18-auth-token.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §10.2.2 AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN request parameter — end-to-end.
tests/18-auth-token.test.ts.description:
Attaches a per-request AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN to SUBSCRIBE and confirms the
relay accepts the extended parameter list. This proves the parity-aware
(length-prefixed odd-key) encoding lands on the wire correctly; deeper
codec round-trip is covered by the unit tests.

The relay may reject the token as unknown/invalid; that's still a valid
exercise of the wire path, so we tolerate REQUEST_ERROR the same way the
SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS e2e test does.

tests/19-subscription-filters.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §10.2.9 SUBSCRIPTION_FILTER — end-to-end against a live relay.
tests/19-subscription-filters.test.ts.description:
Publisher A opens a track; subscriber B subscribes with each filter variant
we expose through `SubscribeOptions.filterType`. The relay is expected to
accept every filter (`SUBSCRIBE_OK`). We keep the deeper "which objects
come back for absolute-range vs. latest" semantics out of scope here — that
depends on relay policy — and only assert the wire-level acceptance so the
codec + session parameter mapping is exercised end-to-end.

tests/20-expires-and-ngr.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §10.2.10 EXPIRES / §10.2.13 NEW_GROUP_REQUEST — end-to-end
tests/20-expires-and-ngr.test.ts.description:
against a live relay.

The relay is expected to accept the SUBSCRIBE and SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS requests
that carry these parameters — we assert wire-level acceptance rather than
higher-level behaviour, which is relay policy dependent. Deeper semantics
(does the relay actually cut a new group on demand? what expiry duration
does it echo back?) live in relay conformance tests.

tests/21-stream-reset.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §11.4.3 stream-reset — end-to-end against a live relay.
tests/21-stream-reset.test.ts.description:
We drive the publisher-side path (calling `resetPublicationStream` while a
subgroup stream is open) and assert the local `stream-reset` event fires
with the requested §15.10.4 code. The subscriber-side path is exercised
opportunistically: if the relay propagates the RESET_STREAM back to the
subscriber, we should see a `stream-reset` there too, but we don't assert
on it since relay behaviour is policy-dependent.

tests/22-padding.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §11.5 padding streams & datagrams — end-to-end against a live relay.
tests/22-padding.test.ts.description:
Sends padding through the wire and confirms:
  • sendPaddingStream() completes without error (relay accepts the reserved
    0x132B3E28 stream type and does not echo it as an object).
  • sendPaddingDatagram() completes without error (relay accepts the
    reserved 0x132B3E29 datagram type). Since datagrams are usually not
    forwarded to other subscribers by relays, we only assert the send
    side succeeds; if a peer *does* receive it, our datagram-manager
    drops it silently — validated in the unit tests.
  • Interleaving padding with a real published object still delivers the
    real object to a subscriber (padding does not clog the pipeline).

tests/23-priority.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §7 priority scheduling — end-to-end against a live relay.
tests/23-priority.test.ts.description:
Two subscribers subscribe to the same track with different subscriber
priorities (§10.2 SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY) and group orders. The publisher
fires objects across a couple of groups; both subscribers must receive
delivery. This exercises the outgoing `sendOrder` path in the publisher
(`deriveSendOrder` → `WebTransportSendStreamOptions.sendOrder`) without
depending on relay-specific priority behaviour.

We don't assert *ordering* of arrival across peers — QUIC scheduling is
inherently best-effort and a relay may reorder freely. We assert:
  • The subscribe with non-default priority + DESCENDING order completes.
  • Both subscribers receive at least one object.
  • Padding does not leak into the delivery path.

tests/25-reserved-namespace.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §3.2.1 — Reserved Namespaces (leading '.', 0x2e).
tests/25-reserved-namespace.test.ts.description:
The client MUST refuse to originate publish / subscribe / fetch under a
track namespace whose first tuple field begins with '.'. This e2e proves
the guard fires *after* a live relay session is established (i.e. it is
not merely a static type check) and that nothing hits the wire — the
relay never sees the reserved request.

tests/26-idle-timeout.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §13.6.1 — Idle Connection handling.
tests/26-idle-timeout.test.ts.description:
§13.6.1 defers idle to QUIC and only recommends periodic PING frames for
long-lived subscriptions. `MOQTSession.configureIdle()` exposes a
keepalive knob that emits §11.5 padding datagrams and a local idle-close
knob. This test proves the keepalive path works against a live relay
(the session survives past the idle threshold when keepalive is on and
closes cleanly with CONTROL_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT when it's not).

Kept small — long real-time waits inflate CI cost. We use a 300ms
idle threshold plus a small `wait()` for the timer to fire.

tests/27-implementation-string.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §13.8 — Fingerprinting mitigation for MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION.
tests/27-implementation-string.test.ts.description:
The client omits the MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION SetupOption by default. Callers can
opt in via `setImplementationString()` before `setup()`. We drive both paths
against a live relay and assert the session completes CLIENT_SETUP <->
SERVER_SETUP either way — the relay MUST ignore MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION and only
fail if the value violates encoding constraints.

tests/28-grease.test.ts.title: Draft-18 §14 Grease — receiver tolerance against a live relay.
tests/28-grease.test.ts.description:
§14 reserves values matching `0x7f * N + 0x9D` across seven registries and
mandates that receivers MUST ignore unknown values (or map unknown error
codes to INTERNAL_ERROR). The Setup Options registry is the easiest to
exercise end-to-end: we advertise a grease key on CLIENT_SETUP and expect
the relay to complete SERVER_SETUP anyway — proving both the relay and our
codec honour the "ignore unknown" rule.

tests/29-subscribe-update-multi-track.te.title: SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE (draft-16) / REQUEST_UPDATE (draft-18) per-request scope.
tests/29-subscribe-update-multi-track.te.description:
Publisher publishes two tracks in the same session. Subscriber subscribes
to both and pauses one. The other track must keep flowing — pause is
scoped to a single subscription's requestId, not the whole session.

This regresses a bug where the publisher-side handler routed forward=0
through `publicationManager.setAllForward(0)`, which flipped every
publication in the session regardless of which subscription paused.

tests/30-room-fanout.test.ts.title: Reproduces the "studio room" topology reported in
tests/30-room-fanout.test.ts.description:
localhost-1790576479222.log — N peers each open a session, subscribe to a
shared room prefix, and announce their own per-peer namespace under it.

The bug report: peer 1 and peer 2 see each other, but peer 3+ never receive
announcements from peers 1/2 (and vice versa). This test asserts that every
peer joining a room learns about every other peer already in the room.

tests/31-room-fanout-tracks.test.ts.title: Second-order studio room reproducer: each peer performs the FULL studio
tests/31-room-fanout-tracks.test.ts.description:
join sequence (subscribe-namespace → publish tracks → announce → and on
namespace-announced from another peer, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS to it).

The bug report says peers 3+ never see peers 1/2's video. Studio's peer
discovery goes:
  1. mediaSession.subscribeNamespace(roomPrefix)
  2. session.publish() for {event, catalog, video, audio} tracks
  3. session.announceNamespace(selfNamespace)
  4. on 'namespace-announced' -> session.subscribeTracks(peerNamespace)
  5. that triggers 'incoming-publish' from the relay for each peer track

This test replays that exact sequence for N peers and asserts each peer
gets an 'incoming-publish' for every OTHER peer's tracks.

tests/32-room-fanout-catalog.test.ts.title: Third-order studio room reproducer: replays the EXACT apps/studio/src/moqt.ts
tests/32-room-fanout-catalog.test.ts.description:
peer wiring — MediaSession.subscribeNamespace + MSFSession.publishCatalog +
mediaSession-managed video/audio publishes + subscribeTracks + catalog
catalog callback via MSFSession.followCatalog.

The bug this exists to catch: the studio UI gates a peer's <canvas> tile on
`peerCatalogs[peerId]` being present and having a track named 'video'. If
MSF catalog delivery fails silently for any peer, that peer's video decodes
fine but is never rendered.

Assertion: every peer's onPeerCatalog callback fires for every OTHER peer,
with a FullCatalog containing 'video' and 'audio' track entries.

tests/33-publish-done.test.ts.title: PUBLISH_DONE on the PUBLISH request stream (draft-18 / draft-22 §9.9).
tests/33-publish-done.test.ts.description:
`unpublish()` sends PUBLISH_DONE as the final message on the PUBLISH
request's bidi stream and then closes it. Sending it on the control
stream instead makes the relay terminate the session, so a follow-up
`publish()` on the same session proves the session survived.

tests/34-draft23.test.ts.title: Draft-23 interop: what draft-23 changed on the wire, against a live relay.
tests/34-draft23.test.ts.description:
Skipped unless MOQT_VERSION=draft-23.

- SETUP over vi64 control framing reaches ready (§9)
- FETCH is answered by REQUEST_OK, not FETCH_OK (§9.3, #2009); the fetch
  stream uses the draft-23 ID rules (§11.4) and its indicators surface as
  `fetch-gap`
- REQUEST_ERROR carries Error Details (§9.4.2); a refusal does not end the session
- Grease Error Details we send are ignored by the relay (§13)

tests/35-publish-forwarding.test.ts.title: Relay forwards a PUBLISH to a matching namespace subscriber.
tests/35-publish-forwarding.test.ts.description:
Draft-18 §6.1 splits discovery in two: SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE asks for
NAMESPACE messages only, and SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS asks for a PUBLISH for every
existing and future track under the prefix (§10.19, §8). Each case opens a
publisher and a subscriber session, has the publisher PUBLISH one track and
send an object every 100 ms, and watches the subscriber for 5 s: did a
PUBLISH arrive (fwdPublish), did its objects follow within 2 s (objects),
and did a NAMESPACE arrive (nsMsg). A plain SUBSCRIBE from a third session
is the control: if it gets objects and the forwarding check fails, the relay
did not forward; if it gets none, the publisher was unreachable and the
case is inconclusive. Each case prints its control-message trace.

MOQ_RELAY_KNOWN_NO_PUBLISH_FWD=1 reports a missing forward without failing,
for a relay with a known gap.

tests/36-request-errors.test.ts.title: Requests the relay cannot serve get a REQUEST_ERROR, not silence.
tests/36-request-errors.test.ts.description:
SUBSCRIBE, FETCH and TRACK_STATUS for a track nobody publishes. Each must be answered within 5 s with
the error code the draft names (DOES_NOT_EXIST, or TIMEOUT once a SUBSCRIBE's
rendezvous timeout runs out), and the session must stay usable afterwards.
A FETCH that starts after the Largest Object, or for a track with no
Objects yet, gets INVALID_RANGE. Draft-22 and later.

tests/37-subscribe-ok-largest.test.ts.title: SUBSCRIBE_OK reports the track's Largest Location.
tests/37-subscribe-ok-largest.test.ts.description:
A subscriber that arrives before any Object is published sees no Largest
Location; one that arrives after groups 0..2 (3 Objects each) were
published sees 2/2, the last Object sent. Draft-22 and later.

tests/38-publish-namespace-lifecycle.tes.title: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE lifecycle, as a namespace subscriber sees it.
tests/38-publish-namespace-lifecycle.tes.description:
A publisher announces a namespace, cancels it, and announces it again. A
session with SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE on the parent prefix must see NAMESPACE,
then NAMESPACE_DONE after the cancel, then NAMESPACE again. The relay
cancelling an announcement on its own cannot be triggered from a client,
so this covers the cancel our side sends and the relay's fan-out of it.
Draft-22 and later.

tests/39-namespace-prefix-update.test.ts.title: REQUEST_UPDATE on a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE changes its prefix.
tests/39-namespace-prefix-update.test.ts.description:
The subscriber watches prefix …/a, then moves it to …/b with
TRACK_NAMESPACE_PREFIX (draft-22 §9.20.20). The relay must answer the
update, stop matching …/a and start matching …/b: a namespace announced
under …/b afterwards arrives, one announced under …/a does not.
Draft-22 and later.

tests/40-concurrent-requests.test.ts.title: Stream-credit flow control, which replaced MAX_REQUEST_ID.
tests/40-concurrent-requests.test.ts.description:
Draft-17 removed MAX_REQUEST_ID: each request now holds a bidirectional
stream, and each subgroup a unidirectional one, so the limits are the QUIC
stream credits the peer grants. Two flows:

- Open requests: one session subscribes to 150 tracks at once. Those over
  the relay's limit must fail quickly and leave the session usable; after
  20 are unsubscribed, 20 new requests must succeed (credit comes back as
  streams close).
- Short-lived streams: 150 groups on one track, one stream each, more than
  a typical initial limit of 100. All must arrive, which needs both sides to
  keep granting unidirectional stream credit.

Draft-22 and later.

tests/41-unknown-parameter.test.ts.title: An unknown Message Parameter closes the session.
tests/41-unknown-parameter.test.ts.description:
Message Parameters are not greased: every one must be defined in the
negotiated version, and an endpoint that receives an unknown one MUST close
the session with INVALID_PARAMETER (draft-23 §9.2; PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
before draft-23). The test builds a TRACK_STATUS with our codec, adds one
parameter of undefined type 0x3C, checks our own decoder rejects only that
parameter, and sends it on a request stream of its own. Draft-22 and later.

tests/42-fill-subscribe.test.ts.title: Fill: a subscriber joining mid-track gets recent history and the live edge.
tests/42-fill-subscribe.test.ts.description:
Draft-22 replaced joining FETCH with FILL_PARAMETERS (§3.4): the relay
opens a fill stream with past groups next to the live subscription. A
holder subscription keeps groups 0..4 in the relay's cache, then:

- SUBSCRIBE with fill of the last 3 groups gets 2..4 from the fill and
  the groups published afterwards (5, 6) live, and nothing before group 2.
- SUBSCRIBE with no fill, then REQUEST_UPDATE with fill of groups 1..2,
  gets exactly groups 1 and 2 from the fill.

Draft-22 and later.

tests/43-fetch-from-cache.test.ts.title: FETCH from the relay's cache, in several shapes.

tests/44-new-group-request.test.ts.title: NEW_GROUP_REQUEST end to end.
tests/44-new-group-request.test.ts.description:
The publisher declares DYNAMIC_GROUPS=1 and keeps sending Objects in group
0, one every 100 ms. The subscriber, which must see DYNAMIC_GROUPS in its
SUBSCRIBE_OK, sends REQUEST_UPDATE with NEW_GROUP_REQUEST. The relay must
pass it to the publisher, which then starts group 1, and group 1 must reach
the subscriber within 3 s. Draft-22 and later.

tests/45-namespace-discovery-flow.test.t.title: Discovery by namespace, then subscription by name: the whole flow.
tests/45-namespace-discovery-flow.test.t.description:
1. Sub sends SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE for a prefix.
2. Pub sends PUBLISH_NAMESPACE for prefix/pub and PUBLISH for its track,
   and sends an Object every 100 ms. It also announces a sibling whose
   last field only starts with the prefix's (…/<id>x/pub): namespaces
   match field by field, so Sub must not see it.
3. Sub gets NAMESPACE for prefix/pub, SUBSCRIBEs to the track by name and
   receives Objects.
4. A late subscriber, Late, sends SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE afterwards and gets
   NAMESPACE for the namespace that already exists.
5. Pub ends the track: Sub gets PUBLISH_DONE.
6. Pub cancels the announcement: Sub and Late get NAMESPACE_DONE.

Draft-22 and later.

tests/46-subscribe-tracks-flow.test.ts.title: SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS and PUBLISH: the whole flow.
tests/46-subscribe-tracks-flow.test.ts.description:
1. Sub sends SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS for a prefix. Pub sends SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS for
   the same prefix too: a relay excludes a subscriber's own tracks
   (draft-22 §6.1), so Pub must never get its own PUBLISH back.
2. Pub publishes tracks a, b and c under prefix/pub and sends Objects on
   each: Sub gets a PUBLISH for each, and their Objects.
3. Pub ends track a: Sub gets PUBLISH_DONE for it.
4. Sub cancels its SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, then Pub publishes track d: the relay
   must not send Sub a PUBLISH for d (draft-22 §6.1).

Draft-22 and later.

tests/47-goaway-flow.test.ts.title: GOAWAY drains a session without breaking what is in flight.
tests/47-goaway-flow.test.ts.description:
GOAWAY does not affect subscription state (draft-23 §9.2): delivery goes
on until the sender ends its requests and closes. A client cannot make the
relay send GOAWAY, so both flows send it from a client, mid-delivery:

- Subscriber sends GOAWAY: Objects keep arriving for 2 s after it, then
  the subscriber unsubscribes and closes with no error from the relay.
- Publisher sends GOAWAY: the subscriber keeps receiving for 2 s, then
  the publisher ends the track and the subscriber gets PUBLISH_DONE, its
  own session untouched.

Draft-22 and later.

tests/48-track-properties.test.ts.title: Track Properties travel from the publisher to every subscriber.
tests/48-track-properties.test.ts.description:
The publisher's PUBLISH carries Track Properties: subgroup delivery
timeout, max cache duration, default publisher priority and group order,
and DYNAMIC_GROUPS. A subscriber must see the same values in its
SUBSCRIBE_OK, and a TRACK_STATUS must report them too (draft-22 §3.7).
Draft-22 and later.

tests/49-object-properties.test.ts.title: Object Properties travel with each Object through the relay.
tests/49-object-properties.test.ts.description:
Every Object the publisher sends carries two Object Properties of types
the relay does not know: 0x40 (even, a varint: group × 100 + object) and
0x41 (odd, bytes: "p<group>/<object>"). Both are below the Mandatory range,
so a relay must forward them unchanged (draft-22 §11.1). The subscriber
checks both on every Object it receives. Draft-22 and later.

tests/50-setup-options-flow.test.ts.title: Setup Options the relay advertises, and one of them honoured in a flow.
tests/50-setup-options-flow.test.ts.description:
SERVER_SETUP carries the relay's Setup Options. Each even option must
hold a varint and each odd one bytes. MAX_REQUEST_UPDATES (draft-22
§9.1.7) bounds the REQUEST_UPDATEs outstanding on one request stream: the
subscriber sends that many at once (at most 4, and 4 when the relay sets
no limit) and every one must get its REQUEST_UPDATE_OK, in order.
Draft-22 and later.

tests.name: CLIENT_SETUP round-trip [chat-stream] > connects, runs setup, reaches ready state
flow: Client: opens WebTransport to the relay
Client: CLIENT_SETUP with the profile draft
Relay → Client: SERVER_SETUP
Check: setup resolves and the session reaches ready
tests.expected: CLIENT_SETUP and SERVER_SETUP complete and the session reaches ready

tests.name: CLIENT_SETUP round-trip [chat-datagram] > connects, runs setup, reaches ready state
flow: Client: opens WebTransport to the relay
Client: CLIENT_SETUP with the profile draft
Relay → Client: SERVER_SETUP
Check: setup resolves and the session reaches ready
tests.expected: CLIENT_SETUP and SERVER_SETUP complete and the session reaches ready

tests.name: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE round-trip [chat-stream] > relay acknowledges announced namespace
